name: Kai Chan
life: “I still remember selling my first whistle to my own uncle.” On Wednesday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Kai knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I sell whistles and dislike giving them away. I loaned my voice for the afternoon instead.
appearance: Kai has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. In conversation Kai gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Kai tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Kai will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To loan a tune without selling an instrument.
family: Rowan Reyes is Kai’s second cousin. Kai sets the time to leave. Rowan picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The housecoat commission*, Rowan says, “I am the neighbor invited last. I promised to dress up until she told me to come straight from work.”
connections: Kai Williams. A rule snapping shut and a borrowed whistle stop the handwritten score sounding too polite.

reactions.situation: An instrument breaks before the fountain piece begins
reactions.response: Kai asks the player whether a different everyday object can carry the missing note.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Kai offers the worker something dry first and leaves it to them whether to pursue the apology.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Kai repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
